How this is resolved

The observation period begins at 12:00 AM ET on Oct 3, 2026 and ends at 11:59 PM ET on Oct 3, 2026.

Truths, ReTruths, and Quote Truths are included in the total count.
Replies are included if captured by Roll Call.
"Between" is inclusive of the lower and upper bound.

Doesn’t count for payout: Posts deleted as of the Expiration Time.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the official vote count is certified.
markets.rules_primary: If at least 132,000,000 valid, blank and null votes, in combination are cast in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The count is the total of voters who voted (comparecimento) in the presidential contest of the first round of Brazil’s 2026 general election, as reported by the Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), including those who cast blank or null votes. Registered voters, abstentions, justified absences and ballots in other contests do not count.

Subject to the contract’s Fully-Conducted Elections and Accelerated Resolution Upon Designated Media Source Declarations provisions, the vote count refers to the officially certified results from the relevant election authority. Provisional, absentee, early, mail-in, or electronic ballots are included only if reflected in the official certification.

The contract resolves based on officially certified results regardless of ongoing appeals. Outside those two contract provisions, preliminary counts, exit polls, projections, or uncertified results do not qualify.

The contract resolves based on officially certified results regardless of ongoing appeals. Outside those two contract provisions, preliminary counts, exit polls, projections, or uncertified results do not qualify.

markets.rules_secondary:
The return for each cryptocurrency in the specified set is calculated independently over the given time period using the formula: Return = (Ending Price − Starting Price) / Starting Price × 100. The Starting Price and Ending Price are defined as the time-weighted average of the Spot Rate values published by CFBenchmarks during the 60-second intervals immediately preceding the start and end of the time period, respectively. Final returns are calculated on an identical basis for every cryptocurrency in the set and rounded to three decimal places (as a percentage).

If two or more cryptocurrencies report an identical return (rounded to three decimal places) such that they are tied for the highest
position, each tied cryptocurrency's Contract will resolve to "Yes" with a value equal to $1 divided by the number of cryptocurrencies tied for the highest position,
rounded down to the nearest cent, and each remaining (non-tied) cryptocurrency's
Contract will resolve to "No."
